description:
We are a team of motivated students with a shared interest in technology, science, and space exploration. Although we come from different backgrounds and have varying levels of experience, we are eager to learn, collaborate, and approach real-world challenges with creativity and analytical thinking.

Our goal is to combine our skills, explore innovative ideas, and develop practical solutions using NASA's open data.
summary:
We have developed a platform, allowing one to see, what crops will grow best, based on location, climate, soil and other NASA data. 

With a straightforward interface, anyone can plan their farm and get data-backed advice on how to plan their farm. 

We plan to scale it to include more crops, and to include more locations and to turn this into a digital platform with more in-depth advice on farm planning and enhancement in the future.
details: The project uses HTML, CSS, and JavaScript for the front-end and Python for the databases. We considered the factors of how NASA data are to be fused together to create predictions and form it into a scoring that a farmer can use for predicting whether they should or should not plant a particular crop. We also used our team member's knowledge in nature science to critically evaluate the output of the database analysis, minimising the biases that may be seen as non-obvious due to the perceived authority of big data. We decided to present it creatively and authentically and would like to embed more of that style in the future of our project.
